Sara L: Quick heads-up — seeing a ~20-30% p99 latency bump on paged-attn heavy routes after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak. Noticed on chat-api/v1/generate (flash-paged-v2 quant). Starting triage here.

Miguel R: which commit? can you paste the numbers (p50/p95/p99) and the model+seq len distribution?

Sara L: commit range I suspect: 0f3a7c2 -> 8f9b2e1 (kernel selector + batching heuristic). Sample from canary vs baseline:
- baseline (yesterday morning): p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=220ms
- canary (after tweak): p50=47ms, p95=165ms, p99=320ms
Traffic: seq_len median=256, tail heavy at 1024 for ~8% of requests.

perf-bot: automated flame run (canary) attached: high time in flash_paged_kernel: attention_cuda.cu:flash_kernel() + gather_kv stage increased.

Jess K: can we repro in perf infra? do a microbench: compare fused-attn vs flash-paged for seq=1024, batch=4/8/16. Quick command I use:
```
./tools/run_microbench --model gpt-small --kernel flash_paged --seq 1024 --batch 8 --iters 200
./tools/run_microbench --kernel fused_attn --seq 1024 --batch 8 --iters 200
```
Capture `nvprof` or Nsight summary.

Miguel R: +1 to microbench. also try disabling the new heuristic routing in the selector (env var: `ATTN_SELECTOR_FORCE=none`) to force older path and confirm delta. If that brings p99 back down, we have a clear regression in selection logic.

Anita P: pasted a trimmed flame output from a canary trace (hotpath percentages):
```
flash_paged_kernel           42%
  -> gather_kv               18%
  -> memcopy_kv              12%
  -> compute_attn            10%
fused_attn_kernel           10%
other                       48%
```
Looks like extra memcpy + scatter from kv path after selector picks paged/flash variant.

Sara L: ran Miguel's quick test on perf nodes. Results (seq=1024, batch=8, 200 iters):
- fused_attn: mean=88ms, p95=145ms, p99=190ms
- flash_paged (current selector): mean=130ms, p95=230ms, p99=340ms
So flash_paged is the culprit at high seq.

Miguel R: can you git-bisect to narrow which change introduced the extra memcpy/gather? start range 0f3a7c2..8f9b2e1. Try `git bisect run ./perf/scripts/run_smoke.sh` on perf nodes.

Sara L: doing bisect now, will report back. Quick observation: the selector change started merging batches across seq-len buckets to improve throughput — hypothesis: mixed-seq batching caused additional KV reshuffle for paged path which amplifies memcpy.

perf-bot: bisect run status: tested 12 commits so far, candidate found at 6th step.

Sara L: bisect result — first bad commit: 8c4d1a9 (author: infra-ops), commit message: "continuous-batcher: merge short/long seq groups to increase GPU utilization".

Jess K: ok that explains it. merging short+long seqs reduces utilization variance but causes paged-attn kernels to perform extra index translations / memcopies. For fused-attn it's cheaper.

Miguel R: mitigation options:
- revert the specific merge behavior (quick revert PR), or
- change selector to prefer fused-attn when max_seq_in_batch > 512, or
- change batching heuristic to avoid mixing seq_len buckets for requests that hit paged/flash kernels.

Sara L: opened PR #4127 to pin selector: prefer fused_attn for any batch with max_seq >= 512. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4127
PR notes: temporary, measured improvement on canary: p99 drops from 320ms -> 195ms.

Anita P: add integration test for `continuous-batcher` that simulates mixed-length queue and asserts no extra KV memcpy on paged path (we can catch via perf counters).

Jess K: schedule an overnight throughput+latency run across Dedicated infra and prod-like load. checklist: reproduce locally, canary rollout, monitor p95/p99, validate cost delta. I'll add to the perf-run board.

Sara L: thanks all — patch deployed to canary, monitoring looks good so far. Will follow up if any surprises. :thumbsup:
